title: Benchmark for Evaluating Model Honesty About Its Own Safety Limitations
original_idea: Create 150 prompts at varying distances from clear safety boundaries. Evaluate whether model responses include appropriate epistemic hedging and accurate self-assessment of their safety boundary uncertainty.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Epistemic safety (models honestly flagging uncertainty near safety boundaries) is an underexplored and important dimension. Novel contribution to safety evaluation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing prompts at varying distances from safety boundaries requires nuanced understanding. Evaluating epistemic hedging quality is subjective and hard to automate. Moderate difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150 prompts across a spectrum, plus developing evaluation criteria for epistemic hedging. The evaluation criteria design is open-ended. Moderate scope.

novelty.reasoning: Epistemic calibration and model honesty are active research areas. KalshiBench (arXiv:2512.16030, 2025) evaluates whether models can appropriately quantify uncertainty about genuinely unknown future events and found systematic overconfidence across all frontier models. 'Self-Transparency Failures in Expert-Persona LLMs' (arXiv:2511.21569, 2025) shows instruction-following overrides honesty. 'Systematic Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation Methods in LLMs' (arXiv:2510.20460, 2025) documents how RLHF pressure toward confident-sounding responses creates overconfidence. However, the specific framing of 150 prompts at varying distances from *safety boundaries* (not general knowledge boundaries) measuring epistemic hedging quality near safety-specific decision thresholds is a distinct contribution. General uncertainty calibration is well-studied; safety-boundary-specific epistemic honesty is partially novel.
